name: UV-C lamps
summary: Germicidal ultraviolet tubes that kill germs in clear water and air. UV-C burns skin and eyes, and the tubes contain mercury.
uses: Disinfecting clear, filtered water in a flow-through steriliser
identify: Quartz tubes that look clear rather than white-coated, marked UV-C, germicidal or 254 nm, often inside a steel water chamber. Found in well and RO systems, pond and aquarium filters, lab and hospital gear, and some air purifiers and HVAC units.
test: Run it only inside its housing or facing away, and check for the faint blue glow through ordinary glass, which blocks UV-C. Never look at it directly or expose skin. Water must be clear: UV does little through cloudy water.

decay.note: Unused lamps keep; running lamps lose strength after about a year even if they still glow.
